newsitem.title: FRANCE: French October jobless slips by surprise 12,000.
newsitem.headline: French October jobless slips by surprise 12,000.

text.p: The number of French unemployed slipped by a surprise 12,000 in October, but the headline number of jobless remained above three million.
The jobless total fell by 12,000 or 0.4 percent to 3,100,800, figures released by the Ministry of Labour on Monday showed.
But the jobless rate according to International Labour Organisation criteria was unchanged at a record 12.6 percent.

The fall was welcome news for the deeply unpopular conservative government of Prime Minister Alain Juppe which has been striving to cut unemployment and at the same time sell its economic austerity programme aimed at qualifying for European monetary union.

"It's clearly better than expected. I was quite encouraged by the figure. It's not going to make a big difference but it does give the government a bit more breathing space," said Joanne Perez, economic strategist at Merrill Lynch.
But economists said that the latest data did not likely herald a reversal of an overall upward trend in unemployment, especially with fourth-quarter economic growth expected to be weak.

David Naude, an economist at JP Morgan, noted that unemployment had risen by nearly 70,000 over the previous two months "and here I think we're seeing the usual volatility, probably paybacks for the strong rises of the past months."

"It's more month-to-month volatility. I really don't thing it signals a change in the overall deterioration although I would have expected unemployment to have risen," said economist Sonja Gibbs of Nomura.
